suite.description: Byte-exact LFCP Wire interoperability vectors: Principals, Control Records, ownership transfer, Key Packages, Data Units, invitation URI, session messages and negative validation cases.
suite.warning: All private keys, DEKs and derived keys in this suite are public test fixtures. They MUST NOT be used in production or as production defaults.

cases.note: Frontier from the accepted Data Units: BOB 1..2 (D1, D2; D3 is past the C6 cutoff) and CAROL 1 (D4).
Frontier with an extra range: the BOB entry of DATA_HAVE_with_hole (1..100, 105..107) and CAROL 1. Not derived from D1-D4.

error.detail: STALE_DATA_EPOCH / quarantine because Bob cutoff at epoch 0 is seq=2

cases.description: D1 sealed under a non-deterministically encoded AAD
cases.note: Client-local rejection (SPEC-PATCH-01 / N3): only a client holding the DEK can detect it; there is no wire error code.

mutation.field: AAD encoding of the actor sequence (seq 1)

rule.text: When an LFCP algorithm requires reconstructing a deterministic structure, such as AEAD AAD, HPKE `info`, or HPKE AAD, the reconstructed structure MUST follow these deterministic CBOR rules exactly. (§26.3: a Data Unit is eligible for merge only if "the unit decrypts successfully"; "A client MUST NOT merge a Data Unit that fails AEAD authentication and SHOULD surface it to the application.")

derivation.why: The receiver reconstructs the canonical AAD, so decryption fails; accepting it would require guessing alternative encodings of signed or authenticated structures.

cases.description: D1 wrapped in COSE_Sign1 tag 18

rule.text: A strict LFCP-WIRE-01 implementation MUST reject a tagged persistent LFCP object as non-canonical, with `MALFORMED_MESSAGE`.

derivation.why: The object ID is SHA-256 of the exact bytes; a tagged copy would be a second, different object for the same content.

cases.description: D1 with one signature bit flipped

rule.text: A receiver MUST reject a signed object whose signature does not verify under the public key of the Principal named by `kid` [...]. It reports `INVALID_SIGNATURE`.

derivation.why: An unverified signature lets anyone inject Data Units in the actor's name.

cases.description: D1 payload signed by CAROL (kid CAROL) instead of the actor BOB

rule.text: A receiver MUST reject a signed object [...] whose `kid` does not identify the Principal the object requires as signer (for example, the actor of a Data Unit). It reports `INVALID_SIGNATURE`.

derivation.why: The signature is valid but by the wrong Principal; accepting it lets one member forge another member's edits.

cases.description: D1 ciphertext sealed under the AAD of sequence 2
cases.note: Client-local rejection (SPEC-PATCH-01 / N3): only a client holding the DEK can detect it; there is no wire error code.

mutation.field: AAD actor sequence used for sealing

rule.text: A Data Unit is eligible for merge only if: [...] 6. the unit decrypts successfully [...] A client MUST NOT merge a Data Unit that fails AEAD authentication and SHOULD surface it to the application.

derivation.why: The AAD binds the ciphertext to its resource, epoch, actor and position; accepting it would let ciphertext be replayed elsewhere.

cases.description: CONTROL_PUT of C6 with expected head C4 while the coordinator head is C5

rule.text: If not equal, it MUST return `NACK(CONTROL_HEAD_MISMATCH)` with the current head.

derivation.why: Compare-and-swap is what keeps the Control Chain linear; committing against a stale head would fork it.

cases.description: PING sent with the unassigned message type 7

rule.text: A message whose type is not assigned in this registry, or is an extension type that was not negotiated for the session, is rejected with `PROTOCOL_UNSUPPORTED`.

derivation.why: A receiver cannot know the body of an unassigned type, so it cannot process the message.

cases.description: CONTROL_PUT of C6 with a null expected head

rule.text: A `CONTROL_PUT` always names an expected head; a null expected head is invalid, because Genesis uses `RESOURCE_HOST`.

derivation.why: Compare-and-swap needs a head to compare against; null would bypass it.

cases.description: DATA_HAVE_with_hole with the extra range written 107..105

rule.text: A range with `start > end`, or one that includes sequence `0`, is rejected with `MALFORMED_MESSAGE`.

derivation.why: Unnormalized live Haves are merged, but a reversed range describes no set of sequences at all.

cases.description: A second Control Record at sequence 6 on top of C5

rule.text: Two different validly signed records referencing the same previous Control Record create a Control Fork. A client MUST NOT silently choose a branch. Neither record is accepted as the Control Head; a receiver that refuses a competing record reports `CONTROL_CONFLICT`.

derivation.why: Choosing a branch silently would let replicas diverge on authorization and keys.

cases.description: C6 with a final frontier of entries CAROL, BOB

rule.text: Field `2` is a canonical frontier (Sections 28.1 and 28.2): canonical `actor-have` entries sorted by raw Principal ID, with at most one entry per Principal. A Key Epoch Record whose final frontier is not canonical MUST be rejected with `MALFORMED_MESSAGE`.

derivation.why: Replicas compute the cutoff from the same frontier bytes; an unsorted frontier would be a second encoding of one cutoff.

cases.description: C6 with a final frontier of entries BOB, BOB

rule.text: Field `2` is a canonical frontier (Sections 28.1 and 28.2): canonical `actor-have` entries sorted by raw Principal ID, with at most one entry per Principal. A Key Epoch Record whose final frontier is not canonical MUST be rejected with `MALFORMED_MESSAGE`.

derivation.why: Two entries for one Principal would make the cutoff ambiguous.

cases.description: C1 with the ability code 2 listed twice

rule.text: An ability list (the abilities and the delegable abilities of a grant, and the abilities of a claim) MUST NOT repeat a code; a record whose list repeats a code is rejected with `MALFORMED_MESSAGE`.

derivation.why: A repeated code makes one grant expressible in several byte forms with different record IDs.

cases.description: C9 granting data/write, which the parent grant C8 cannot delegate

rule.text: If `parent grant id` is present: [...] every granted ability MUST be included in the parent's delegable abilities;

derivation.why: Delegation can only narrow authority; a child granting more than its parent may delegate would escalate it.

cases.description: CAROL revokes C7, the grant she received, instead of C9

rule.text: The owner may revoke any grant. Otherwise, revoke authority **covers** a grant when the revoker issued it, or when it was delegated, directly or through further delegations, from a grant the revoker issued. A grant the revoker received is not covered unless the revoker also issued one of its ancestors.

derivation.why: Holding capability/revoke lets a member undo what it delegated, not the grants others gave it.

cases.description: CAROL revokes C9 a second time, after C10

mutation.field: position: Control Sequence and previous record

rule.text: Revoking a grant that is already revoked is rejected with `AUTHORIZATION_FAILED`.

derivation.why: A second revocation has no effect to apply; rejecting it keeps every committed record meaningful.

cases.description: CAROL revokes a grant ID that names no grant of the chain, instead of C9

rule.text: A revocation is checked in this order, and each failure is rejected with `AUTHORIZATION_FAILED`: 1. the target grant ID MUST name a grant of this Control Chain; revoking a grant that does not exist fails;

derivation.why: A revocation of nothing has no authority to check against; accepting it would put a meaningless record in the chain.

cases.description: C5 with route version 0, the version Genesis already implies

rule.text: Each Route Update MUST carry a route version strictly greater than the current one: `0` after Genesis (Section 15), otherwise the version of the last committed Route Update. A Route Update whose issuer lacks `route/update`, or whose route version is not greater, is rejected with `AUTHORIZATION_FAILED`.

derivation.why: A route version that does not advance could replace the current route with an older one.

cases.description: C0 issued and signed by BOB while its body names OWNER as owner

rule.text: The Genesis Record MUST be signed by the owner Principal contained in the body. A Genesis Record whose issuer or `kid` is not that owner is rejected with `INVALID_SIGNATURE`.

derivation.why: Genesis establishes the owner; a Genesis signed by anyone else would let them claim a Resource in another name.

cases.description: A second, different Genesis for the same Resource ID

rule.text: Two different validly signed Genesis Records for one Resource ID are a fork at the root, handled the same way: neither is accepted, and the Resource is in `CONTROL_CONFLICT`.

derivation.why: Genesis has no previous record, so without this rule two roots would not count as a fork.

cases.description: C0 with an http:// sync endpoint

rule.text: A receiver MUST reject a record carrying such a URL with any scheme other than `ws` or `wss` with `MALFORMED_MESSAGE`.

derivation.why: Endpoints carry LFCP over WebSocket; any other scheme cannot be reached as an LFCP endpoint.

cases.description: C1 with the reserved core Control Record type 9

rule.text: Unknown core Control Record types MUST cause validation failure, with `INVALID_CONTROL_CHAIN`.

derivation.why: A core type the receiver does not know may carry authority it cannot evaluate; accepting it would let replicas disagree on the chain.

cases.description: C1 replaced by an extension-type (32) record issued by BOB
cases.note: Structurally valid: the typed CDDL admits extension types 32 and above (SPEC-PATCH-03 / W2). The owner-authority failure is AUTHORIZATION_FAILED (SPEC-PATCH-04 / general code rule).

mutation.to: type 32 issued and signed by BOB

rule.text: A Control Record of an extension type (`32` or above) requires owner authority: its issuer MUST be the Resource owner at the record's position in the chain, whether or not the receiver supports the extension.

derivation.why: Extension records share the chain with core records; letting a non-owner append them would let any member fork or extend the chain with records other replicas cannot evaluate.

cases.description: D1 re-issued with actor sequence 0

rule.text: Sequence numbers begin at `1`. A receiver MUST reject a Data Unit with actor sequence `0` with `MALFORMED_MESSAGE`.

derivation.why: Sequence 0 is outside the per-actor sequence space, so Have Vectors and hash chains cannot describe it.

cases.description: D1 with a previous-unit reference although it is sequence 1

rule.text: For sequence `1`, it MUST be `null`. [...] A gap or mismatch MUST be reported to the sync engine.

derivation.why: The actor hash chain must start at sequence 1; a non-null link there breaks gap and equivocation detection.

cases.description: A package naming CAROL at C3, where she is authorized, sealed to BOB
cases.note: Client-local rejection (SPEC-PATCH-01 / N5): the package is ignored and surfaced; there is no wire error code.

mutation.field: recipient and Control Head (payload fields 2 and 3), sealed to BOB

rule.text: The HPKE `info` value is deterministic CBOR encoding of ["LFCP-KEY-v1", resource-id, data epoch, recipient]. [...] A package that does not open for its named recipient, or whose DEK does not match the commitment, is ignored and SHOULD be surfaced to the application. This is a client-local decision [...]

derivation.why: HPKE info binds the recipient; a package that does not open for its named recipient delivers no key.

cases.description: KP0 with a 31-byte HPKE enc

rule.text: With that suite `enc` is the 32-byte ephemeral X25519 public key, and the ciphertext is the 32-byte DEK followed by the 16-byte Poly1305 tag. (CDDL: `5 => bstr .size 32` and `6 => bstr .size 48`.)

derivation.why: With the fixed suite every enc is a 32-byte X25519 key; any other length is structurally invalid and detectable without opening the package.

cases.description: SNAPSHOT-01 with a frontier that violates §28.1 rule 2

rule.text: 2. key `2` MUST be omitted when there are no extra ranges; (§28.2: "A Snapshot verifier MUST reject a Snapshot whose frontier is not canonical, with `MALFORMED_MESSAGE`.")

derivation.why: Snapshot AAD and signature cover the frontier bytes, so replicas must agree on exactly one encoding of a frontier.

cases.description: SNAPSHOT-02 with a frontier that violates §28.1 rule 4

rule.text: 4. each sequence range MUST have `start <= end`; (§28.2: "A Snapshot verifier MUST reject a Snapshot whose frontier is not canonical, with `MALFORMED_MESSAGE`.")

derivation.why: Snapshot AAD and signature cover the frontier bytes, so replicas must agree on exactly one encoding of a frontier.

cases.description: SNAPSHOT-02 with a frontier that violates §28.1 rule 5

rule.text: 5. ranges MUST be strictly above `contiguous`; (§28.2: "A Snapshot verifier MUST reject a Snapshot whose frontier is not canonical, with `MALFORMED_MESSAGE`.")

derivation.why: Snapshot AAD and signature cover the frontier bytes, so replicas must agree on exactly one encoding of a frontier.

cases.description: SNAPSHOT-02 with a frontier that violates §28.1 rule 5

rule.text: 5. ranges MUST be strictly above `contiguous`; the first range MUST start at or above `contiguous + 2`, because a range starting at `contiguous + 1` extends the contiguous prefix and is absorbed into `contiguous`; (§28.2: "A Snapshot verifier MUST reject a Snapshot whose frontier is not canonical, with `MALFORMED_MESSAGE`.")

derivation.why: Snapshot AAD and signature cover the frontier bytes, so replicas must agree on exactly one encoding of a frontier.

cases.description: SNAPSHOT-02 with a frontier that violates §28.1 rule 6

rule.text: 6. ranges MUST be sorted by ascending `start`, then ascending `end`; (§28.2: "A Snapshot verifier MUST reject a Snapshot whose frontier is not canonical, with `MALFORMED_MESSAGE`.")

derivation.why: Snapshot AAD and signature cover the frontier bytes, so replicas must agree on exactly one encoding of a frontier.

cases.description: SNAPSHOT-02 with a frontier that violates §28.1 rule 7

rule.text: 7. ranges MUST be non-overlapping; (§28.2: "A Snapshot verifier MUST reject a Snapshot whose frontier is not canonical, with `MALFORMED_MESSAGE`.")

derivation.why: Snapshot AAD and signature cover the frontier bytes, so replicas must agree on exactly one encoding of a frontier.

cases.description: SNAPSHOT-02 with a frontier that violates §28.1 rule 8

rule.text: 8. ranges MUST be non-adjacent; (§28.2: "A Snapshot verifier MUST reject a Snapshot whose frontier is not canonical, with `MALFORMED_MESSAGE`.")

derivation.why: Snapshot AAD and signature cover the frontier bytes, so replicas must agree on exactly one encoding of a frontier.

cases.description: SNAPSHOT-01 with a frontier that violates §28.1 rule 9

rule.text: 9. no two `actor-have` entries for the same Principal MAY occur in one canonical frontier. (§28.2: "A Snapshot verifier MUST reject a Snapshot whose frontier is not canonical, with `MALFORMED_MESSAGE`.")

derivation.why: Snapshot AAD and signature cover the frontier bytes, so replicas must agree on exactly one encoding of a frontier.

cases.description: SNAPSHOT-01 with CAROL listed before BOB

rule.text: Entries MUST be sorted by ascending raw 32-byte `principal-id`, compared lexicographically as unsigned bytes. [...] A Snapshot verifier MUST reject a Snapshot whose frontier is not canonical, with `MALFORMED_MESSAGE`.

derivation.why: Snapshot AAD and signature cover the frontier bytes, so replicas must agree on exactly one entry order.

cases.description: SNAPSHOT-01 with Snapshot Sequence 0

rule.text: Snapshot Sequences begin at `1`.

derivation.why: Sequence 0 is outside the publisher sequence space, as for actor sequences (§8).

cases.description: A Snapshot of epoch 0 whose frontier covers BOB 1..3, beyond the C6 cutoff (BOB 2)

mutation.field: Data Epoch, Control Head and frontier

rule.text: A Snapshot MUST NOT include Data Units beyond a closed epoch's cutoff. When the Snapshot's Data Epoch has been closed by a Key Epoch Record the verifier knows, every sequence its frontier covers MUST lie within that record's final frontier (Section 19.1); a verifier rejects a Snapshot whose frontier covers any unit beyond it with `STALE_DATA_EPOCH`.

derivation.why: A Snapshot that includes stale work would merge it into every replica that loads it, bypassing the cutoff.

cases.description: CAROL Data Unit in closed epoch 0, where C6 records no CAROL entry

rule.text: If an actor is absent from the recorded frontier, no newly discovered Data Units from that actor in the closed epoch are automatically acceptable. Any later-arriving previous-epoch unit beyond that frontier MUST NOT be merged automatically. A server that receives such a unit in `DATA_PUT` responds `NACK(STALE_DATA_EPOCH)`; a client keeps it in quarantine. [...] It SHOULD be surfaced to the application as stale offline work [...]

derivation.why: The cutoff frontier makes revocation deterministic; merging late closed-epoch work would let removed members keep writing.

cases.description: D1 payload with a non-shortest integer encoding, re-signed

mutation.field: payload encoding of the data epoch (0)

rule.text: A receiver MUST also reject a persistent signed object whose protected-header bytes or payload bytes are not the deterministic encoding of their own decoded value. [...] any difference is rejected with `MALFORMED_MESSAGE`.

derivation.why: Two byte forms of one payload would be two objects with different IDs for the same content.

cases.description: BOB Principal Descriptor with an additional field 3

rule.text: A Principal Descriptor with any field other than `0`, `1` and `2` is invalid; the map is closed, as the CDDL above defines it.

derivation.why: An open descriptor would let two byte forms describe one Principal and carry unauthenticated data next to its keys.

error.detail: AUTH_FAILED when received in HELLO or AUTH (LFCP-WIRE-01 §7)

cases.description: D1 signed with a small-order R that cofactored (ZIP-215) verification accepts

rule.text: A verifier MUST reject the signature, with `INVALID_SIGNATURE`, when any of the following holds: [...] 3. `A` or `R` is a point of small order;

derivation.why: R is the neutral element and S = k·a, so both the cofactorless and the cofactored equations hold; only the small-order rule makes every implementation reject it alike.

cases.description: Principal Descriptor whose Ed25519 key is a point of small order

mutation.field: Ed25519 public key (field 1), with the ID recomputed

rule.text: A receiver MUST also validate the Ed25519 public key in field `1` whenever a descriptor is received: it MUST be a canonical point encoding and MUST NOT be a point of small order, as defined in Section 10.5.1. A descriptor whose key fails this check is invalid.

derivation.why: A small-order key admits signatures that verify for many messages; rejecting it at receipt keeps such a Principal out of every authorization decision.

error.detail: AUTH_FAILED when received in HELLO or AUTH (LFCP-WIRE-01 §7)

cases.description: CAROL seq 4 linked to seq 2 across the abandoned seq 3
cases.note: Receive accepted_seq1_cose, then accepted_seq2_cose, then cose_sign1. All three are accepted; the Have Vector keeps the hole: CAROL 1..2 plus 4..4.

cases.description: CAROL seq 4 whose previous names a unit the receiver does not have
cases.note: Receive accepted_seq1_cose, then accepted_seq2_cose, then cose_sign1: it is held (reported), not merged.

rule.text: A unit links when its `previous` names the receiver's latest accepted unit of that actor [...], even when sequences lie between the two. Such a sequence gap is a hole: it never blocks the chain [...]. A unit that does not link MUST be reported to the sync engine and is held, not merged, until it links [...]

derivation.why: Only a link to the latest accepted unit completes the chain; a link to an unknown unit waits for it.

cases.description: The bearer URI with an undefined query parameter
cases.note: It parses to the same Resource, endpoint, grant and secret as invite_uri.

cases.description: The bearer URI with its grant parameter repeated
cases.note: Client-local rejection: no wire code.

rule.text: A receiver ignores query parameters this section does not define, for forward compatibility, but rejects a URI whose query is not well-formed percent-encoding, that repeats `grant`, or whose `endpoint` or `grant` values are invalid.

derivation.why: Two grant values are ambiguous: the receiver cannot tell which grant the secret is for.

cases.description: CAROL seq 4 naming seq 2, which the server stores
cases.note: Rule 1: `previous` is a stored unit of the actor at a lower sequence.

cases.description: CAROL seq 4 naming seq 2, which the server lost
cases.note: The server stores only seq 1: no rule holds. NACK details: the `previous` of seq 4.

rule.text: A server MUST refuse a Data Unit whose `previous` is not `null` unless [...] the server stores a unit of that actor, at a sequence below `N`, whose Data Unit ID is `previous` [...]; an earlier unit of the same `DATA_PUT` is such a unit [...]; a Snapshot the server stores covers sequence `m` of that actor in its frontier, with `m < N`, and the server stores no unit of that actor at a sequence between `m` and `N`.

derivation.why: Accepting seq 4 would serve a unit that no receiver can link (§26.2).

cases.description: CAROL seq 2 and seq 4 in one DATA_PUT, in that order
cases.note: Rule 2: seq 2, earlier in the same DATA_PUT, is the `previous` of seq 4.

cases.description: CAROL seq 4 before seq 2 in one DATA_PUT
cases.note: Units are evaluated in message order: seq 4 comes first and its `previous` is unknown; the DATA_PUT is all-or-nothing (§51), so seq 2 is not stored either.

rule.text: A server MUST refuse a Data Unit whose `previous` is not `null` unless [...] the server stores a unit of that actor, at a sequence below `N`, whose Data Unit ID is `previous` [...]; an earlier unit of the same `DATA_PUT` is such a unit [...]; a Snapshot the server stores covers sequence `m` of that actor in its frontier, with `m < N`, and the server stores no unit of that actor at a sequence between `m` and `N`.

derivation.why: Only an earlier unit of the same DATA_PUT counts.

cases.description: CAROL seq 4 naming one unit of an equivocating pair at seq 2
cases.note: The server keeps both seq 2 units as evidence (§26.2); either counts as a stored unit.

cases.description: CAROL seq 4 naming seq 2, covered by a stored Snapshot frontier
cases.note: Rule 3: the Snapshot covers CAROL 1..2 (m = 2 < 4) and the server stores no CAROL unit above 2.

cases.description: CAROL seq 4 naming seq 2 when the Snapshot covers only seq 1 and another seq 2 is stored
cases.note: Rule 3 fails: the server stores a CAROL unit at seq 2, between m = 1 and 4, and it is not the `previous` of seq 4.

rule.text: A server MUST refuse a Data Unit whose `previous` is not `null` unless [...] the server stores a unit of that actor, at a sequence below `N`, whose Data Unit ID is `previous` [...]; an earlier unit of the same `DATA_PUT` is such a unit [...]; a Snapshot the server stores covers sequence `m` of that actor in its frontier, with `m < N`, and the server stores no unit of that actor at a sequence between `m` and `N`.

derivation.why: A stored unit between the frontier and N shows that the frontier does not stand for the missing predecessor.

cases.description: CAROL seq 3 with a null previous while seq 1 and 2 are stored
cases.note: A null `previous` is not checked by §51.1: a writer with no accepted unit of its own names null (§26.2).

cases.description: Contiguous Have Vectors; each side lacks something
cases.note: Local BOB 1..100 and CAROL 1..8; remote BOB 1..104.

cases.description: Have Vectors with holes on both sides
cases.note: Local BOB 1..100 plus 105..107; remote BOB 1..102 plus 106..110.

cases.description: Equal Have Vectors
cases.note: Nothing to request and nothing to offer.

cases.description: A server whose store lost the latest unit
cases.note: The drill of ADR 0008: the client holds CAROL 1..4, the restored server CAROL 1..3. The client offers 4 before it writes 5 (§68.1).

cases.description: RFC 8032 §7.1 TEST 1: a valid signature over the empty message
cases.note: External standard vector (RFC 8032 §7.1 TEST 1).

cases.description: TEST 1 with S = L

rule.text: 1. `S` is not less than the group order `L`;

derivation.why: S must be reduced: S = L would let one signature have several encodings.

cases.description: TEST 1 with S + L in place of S

rule.text: 1. `S` is not less than the group order `L`;

derivation.why: S + L satisfies the equation like S; accepting it makes signatures malleable.

cases.description: TEST 1 with the public key A encoded as y = p + 1

rule.text: 2. `A` or `R` is not a canonical point encoding: its `y` coordinate is not less than `p`, it is not a point of the curve, or `x = 0` with the sign bit set;

derivation.why: A non-canonical key encoding gives one Principal several key byte strings.

cases.description: TEST 1 with R encoded as y = p + 1

rule.text: 2. `A` or `R` is not a canonical point encoding: its `y` coordinate is not less than `p`, it is not a point of the curve, or `x = 0` with the sign bit set;

derivation.why: A non-canonical R gives one signature several byte strings.

cases.description: TEST 1 with the public key A = (x = 0, y = 1) and the sign bit set

rule.text: 2. `A` or `R` is not a canonical point encoding: its `y` coordinate is not less than `p`, it is not a point of the curve, or `x = 0` with the sign bit set;

derivation.why: x = 0 has no sign; a set sign bit is a second encoding of the same point.

cases.description: TEST 1 with R = (x = 0, y = 1) and the sign bit set

rule.text: 2. `A` or `R` is not a canonical point encoding: its `y` coordinate is not less than `p`, it is not a point of the curve, or `x = 0` with the sign bit set;

derivation.why: x = 0 has no sign; a set sign bit is a second encoding of the same point.

cases.description: TEST 1 with the public key A = the neutral element

rule.text: 3. `A` or `R` is a point of small order;

derivation.why: A small-order key admits signatures that verify for many messages.

cases.description: A mixed-order key A = [a]B + T8 that the cofactored equation accepts
cases.note: Constructed: a = 0x1234567890abcdef * 977 mod L, T8 a point of order 8, R = [7777]B, the first message "mixed-order N" with k mod 8 != 0, S = 7777 + k*a mod L. A is not itself of small order; cofactored verification accepts it.

cases.description: R = the neutral element with S = k*a, which both equations accept
cases.note: Constructed: a = 0x1234567890abcdef * 977 mod L, A = [a]B, R = the neutral element, S = k*a mod L for the message "small-order R".
